assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production background panorama for an original pixel-art Vancouver side-scrolling portfolio game. Create one exceptionally beautiful wide 3:1 panoramic landscape, clean authentic hand-placed 16-bit pixel art, SNES-era adventure game background, hard square pixel clusters with restrained dithering, no blur or anti-aliasing. The imaginary journey runs along Vancouver's waterfront: on the left ancient dark evergreen cedars of Stanley Park frame a sparkling blue-green inlet, layered coastal mountains with snow patches span the horizon, the recognizable green Lions Gate suspension bridge crosses from the wooded left peninsula toward the centre, and a small Vancouver glass-tower skyline and white Canada Place sails on the far right. Spring wildflowers and warm brown shoreline rocks at the edges. Quiet pale mint sky occupies the upper 38 percent, soft cream peach clouds, sunlit sage foothills, teal water with bright pixel reflections. Clear afternoon after rain, peaceful, nostalgic, adventurous, rich environmental detail and carefully shaded rocks and vegetation. Side-on game composition with distant mountains and water filling most of the frame; absolutely no close foreground path covering the bottom; leave the lower middle as open water because a walking trail will be composited by game code. No text, no lettering, no interface, no border, no characters, no people, no logos, no watermark. Wide cinematic landscape composition, NOT isometric, NOT photorealistic, NOT vector illustration. Polished videogame environment art.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent game sprite asset: one majestic Pacific Northwest western red cedar tree, full tree from tip to root, isolated on genuinely transparent background, centred, fills 90% of a tall portrait canvas. Exceptional authentic detailed 16-bit pixel art with hard square pixel clusters, crisp stepped outlines, restrained dithering, deep forest green shadow foliage, sunlit sage olive needles, warm brown deeply ridged trunk. Many irregular layered lateral boughs and hanging sprays of foliage, natural asymmetric canopy wider in bottom half, slightly visible trunk near base. Tiny ferns and exposed roots at the bottom. Front/side view for a side-scrolling Vancouver waterfront adventure game, no perspective ground plane. Cohesive soft afternoon light, retro adventure-game aesthetic. Absolutely no sky, no background color, no cast shadow outside the tree, no frame, no text, no character. Not smooth vector art, not 3D, not photorealistic. Pixel edges throughout.

Use case: stylized-concept / geographic correction.
Create a replacement wide 3:1 pixel-art game background. Use the supplied image ONLY as a reference for the crisp 16-bit pixel technique, nostalgic afternoon atmosphere and mint/teal palette. Its geography is WRONG and must be completely recomposed.

PRIMARY REQUIREMENT: A geographically coherent oblique panoramic view of Vancouver from an elevated offshore position WEST OF FIRST NARROWS, looking EAST / EAST-SOUTHEAST into Burrard Inlet. Think of a convincing simplified aerial landscape, not a montage of landmarks.

There must be TWO clearly separated continuous shores:
LEFT (NORTH SIDE): West Vancouver's waterfront occupies the nearer left shoreline, with low-rise waterfront buildings, houses and leafy residential hills; North Vancouver continues farther away on the SAME left/north shore, with some modest apartment buildings and urban waterfront detail. North Shore foothills rise behind these communities on the LEFT ONLY, with restrained spring snow patches higher on Cypress/Grouse/Lions-region peaks. Do not depict the left shoreline as Stanley Park. It is inhabited North/West Vancouver, visibly with buildings.
RIGHT (SOUTH SIDE): Stanley Park is a broad wooded HEADLAND on the near right, with a low cliff and seawall tracing its waterside edge. This park is unmistakably one CONTINUOUS PENINSULA connected to the West End and DOWNTOWN VANCOUVER farther to the right/back. Show a broad visible continuous land connection transitioning from park canopy to urban streets and the compact glass-tower skyline. No water gap or channel between Stanley Park and downtown. The downtown skyline has no tall alpine mountains directly behind it; pale open sky there.
MIDDLE WATER: Burrard Inlet is an open blue-green channel between the northern left shore and the southern right peninsula. It recedes east into the image centre.
LIONS GATE BRIDGE: exactly ONE slender green suspension bridge with two towers, crosses the narrow water from the LEFT North Shore to Prospect Point on the RIGHT Stanley Park headland. Its SOUTHERN approach visibly goes into Stanley Park forest, not into skyscrapers and not to a floating wooded island. Bridge sits mid-distance and should not obstruct the clear two-shore layout.
Small recognizable Vancouver buildings beyond the park on the right; Canada Place sails may be very small along the inner harbour on that same downtown side if visible naturally from this perspective, never isolated offshore. Do not force large sails if perspective makes them occluded.

COMPOSITION: Wide panoramic side-scrolling scenery, top 35 percent mostly quiet pale mint sky for webpage text, lower quarter open sparkling water, park and skyline on right connected in depth, near left modest urban waterfront, mountains left/background. No close foreground framing tree, no giant individual trees at either edge, no foreground bushes, no foreground path, no character, no UI, no labels, no text, no borders. Only the natural distant tree canopy in the real park and on the North Shore hills. Mature polished detailed retro pixel art, small hard-edged square pixel clusters, no blur, no vector style, no photorealistic finish. Preserve the reference's beautiful pixel technique but REPLACE ITS INCORRECT GEOGRAPHIC COMPOSITION.
